title: Where Words Come From
summary: How languages change, borrow words and keep growing, with Tamil and English examples.

steps.title: Languages are alive
sentences: Languages change over time, just like people do.
New words come when we need them, like 'selfie' or 'online'.
Old words fade when we stop using them.

steps.title: Borrowed words
sentences: English has borrowed words from many languages, including Tamil.
The words 'catamaran', 'curry', 'cheroot' and 'mango' are all believed to come from Tamil.
Tamil, in turn, uses words like 'bus', 'school' and 'computer' from English.

steps.title: Word parts
sentences: Many English words are built from roots, prefixes and suffixes.
For example 'un' means not, 'happy' is the root, so 'unhappy' means not happy.
Knowing common parts helps you guess new words.

steps.title: Language families
sentences: Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam belong to the Dravidian family.
Hindi, Bengali and English belong to the large Indo-European family.

facts: Tamil is among the world's oldest surviving classical languages and has literature more than two thousand years old.
India's Constitution lists 22 official languages in the Eighth Schedule.
The English word 'orange' came through several languages from a Sanskrit and Dravidian source word.

quiz.q: Which English word comes from Tamil?
quiz.why: Catamaran comes from the Tamil word kattumaram.
